timeline.plain: Staff told Council how they would build the 2027 budget and when Council would see it.

timeline.title: Online budget survey and quiz on EngageWR
timeline.plain: Anyone can tell the Region what matters most to them in the 2027 budget by filling in the online survey or quiz. The prize draw for taking part runs until February 26, 2027.

participation.instructions: Fill in the 2027 Plan and Budget survey or quiz on EngageWR. You can also post ideas and questions there. The prize draw linked to the survey closes at 11:59 pm on Friday, February 26, 2027.

timeline.title: The Regional Chair gets strong-mayor budget powers
timeline.plain: From today the Region of Waterloo is on Ontario's list of strong-mayor municipalities. Its head of council, the Regional Chair (now appointed by the province), gets the job of proposing the Region's budget. Council can still change it.

timeline.title: Regional Council: 2027 Plan and Budget Overview
timeline.plain: The Region's budget page lists this as the first look at the 2027 budget for the new Council. You can ask to speak to Council or write to them. Under the new strong-chair rules the Regional Chair proposes the budget, and only in 2027, so how this meeting fits that process has not been published yet.

participation.instructions: Register as a delegation with the Regional Clerk. Register by noon one week before the meeting to be listed on the agenda and get 5 minutes. Register at least 24 hours before to still get 5 minutes; later than that you get 3 minutes. Send any slides or handouts at least 24 hours before.

Send a written submission to Council through the Regional Clerk's Office. Written submissions are public: they are attached to the meeting agenda or minutes. Questions about the online budget feedback go to 2027PlanAndBudget@regionofwaterloo.ca.
Council meetings are streamed live and recorded on the Region's website.

timeline.title: Earliest day the Chair can propose the 2027 budget
timeline.plain: Because 2026 was an election year, the Chair can propose the 2027 budget only in 2027, not before.

timeline.title: Deadline for the Regional Chair to propose the 2027 budget
timeline.plain: The Chair must give the proposed budget to Council and make it public by February 1. If the Chair does not, Council prepares and adopts the budget itself. Before then, tell the Chair and your councillors what you want in it.

participation.instructions: Write to the Regional Chair and to Regional Council through the Regional Clerk's Office. Under the strong-chair rules the Chair writes the proposed budget, so the Chair is the person to tell what you want in it. Written submissions to Council are public.
Contact your regional councillors. Council can change the Chair's budget only by voting within its time limit, and can overturn a veto only with a two-thirds vote.

timeline.title: Deadline for councillors' budget motions
timeline.plain: Last day for councillors to put forward changes to the budget. To ask your councillor to propose a change, contact them before this date.

participation.instructions: Contact your regional councillor before February 15, 2027 if you want them to propose a change to the budget.

citation.quote: February 15, 2027 - Deadline for submission of Councillor motions

timeline.title: Council's 30 days to change the budget (ends 3 March 2027 at the latest)
timeline.plain: Council has 30 days from getting the Chair's budget to vote on changes. If the Chair proposes on February 1, the last day is March 3, 2027; it is earlier if the budget comes sooner or Council shortens the time. If Council makes no changes, the budget is adopted. This is when speaking to Council matters most.

timeline.plain: After Council's 30 days, the Chair has up to 10 days to veto changes Council made, in writing with reasons. If the Chair does not veto, the budget with Council's changes is adopted.
